title: Make the steward a model-backed, read-only agent that queues work
summary: Retry of the rejected steward job: replace the failure-counting steward with an AgentDriver run using the stored STEWARD_PROMPT, read-only access to Athena's code, records, git log and GitHub CI/PRs/deploys, and queue its items through decide(). This time the gh policy denies every field/method flag form (including attached `-ftitle=x`), and each criterion is exercised by a test. The audience is the Athena owner.

defaults_applied.how: Policy and steward tests added; cargo test and clippy pass.
Each criterion is exercised by a fake-driver test before finishing.
Policy denies the whole class of attached field flags, not just -ftitle; blind-spot keys made stable.
Read-only access is enforced by the tool policy, with tests.
Docs and CHANGELOG explain the change for outside readers.
Recovered the goal from the earlier attempt and findings.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The new request is 'try again': the original goal and accepted reading stand, plus the earlier verifier's findings must be fixed.
Steward git-history access stays a log file of recent commits plus the one-commit snapshot, because private paths are hidden; the limit is documented.
The steward may borrow the verifier's model/budget unless a steward-specific setting is cheap to add; this is noted in the docs.
Blind-spot keys use a stable source name, not error text, so repeated failures dedupe.
Extra files touched by the last attempt (store.rs steward_runs, test helpers handling Role::Steward) are allowed and are listed as deliverables this time.

acceptance_criteria.text: steward::run invokes an AgentDriver with STEWARD_PROMPT as the system prompt and records the invocation (role, usage, cost) like other roles; note_finished still runs it in the background without blocking.

The gh policy in policy.rs is allow-list based for flags: any word starting with -f/-F (attached forms like -ftitle=x, -Fx=@f), --field, --raw-field, -X/--method other than GET, --input, and mutating git/gh commands are denied; unit tests cover these denied forms and the allowed reads (gh run list/view, gh pr list/view, gh api GET).

Agent output is structured work items (kind, key, title, rung, source and evidence refs, request text); Athena validates it and routes every item through decide(): rungs at or below the limit queue a Request, higher rungs queue only a proposal with evidence.

Each unreadable source (including GitHub unavailable) becomes a blind-spot item whose key uses only the stable source name, not error text; items whose key already exists in records are not queued twice.

The old repeated_failures counting is removed or passed to the agent as input; docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and CHANGELOG.md say the steward now calls a model and state the git-history and model/budget limits.

Run `cargo test`: crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs with the fake driver shows (a) scripted output with a real gap commits the work item and a queued request, (b) empty output makes no commit, (c) a second run with the same keys queues nothing again, (d) a nested run makes no real model call, and (e) the fake agent's recorded reads cover the named sources (jobs, events, introspections, class registry, decisions, git log).
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Giving the steward write access to GitHub, git, or the repository.
Exposing private paths or full git object history to the agent.
Changing the requirements ladder rungs or the steward cadence.
A separate steward model/budget configuration (only noted as future work).
departures: Larger than the reference: the earlier attempt touched about 22 files across 7 crates, so cost and time are well above typical jobs; acceptance risk is a bit lower since the reading was accepted before.
